title: Evidence sync handoff protocol and error-mode playbook
body:
Purpose:

This doc captures a pragmatic handoff protocol for automated evidence streams between collectors, the evidence orchestration layer, and downstream SIEM/export sinks. It focuses on minimizing lost evidence, ensuring provable delivery semantics (at-least-once with dedup safeguards), and defining operator playbooks for common error modes.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, security engineers, compliance engineers, solutions eng who operate or onboard evidence pipelines.
- Scope: Collector -> Orchestrator -> Evidence Store -> SIEM/Export microservices; includes retry/backoff, idempotency, RBAC considerations, and verification checks. Not covering agent install or kernel-level forensics collection.

Goals and constraints:
- Guarantee durable handoff for control-evidence assets required by audits (e.g., access grants, role changes, key rotations).
- Keep end-to-end latency within SLA targets for realtime alerts (<30s median for high-priority audit events) while supporting batch backfill.
- Support mixed export modes: streaming (Kafka/HTTP) and batched S3 snapshots for long-tail exports.
- Work within existing RBAC v2 permission model: collectors have scoped write tokens, orchestrator has elevated export consent audited by KMS.

Key concepts and components:
- Collector: runs in customer infra or hosted sidecar, emits event envelopes to orchestrator endpoint.
- Orchestrator: durable queue + dispatcher that coordinates verification, enrichment, and export. Handles routing policies (by priority, region, customer tier).
- Evidence Store: append-only storage used for TTLed retention and replay/backfill.
- Export Sink(s): SIEM connectors, S3 exports, downstream legal/forensics endpoints.
- Control Evidence Envelope: stable JSON envelope used across system for routing and verification.

Control Evidence Envelope (recommended fields):
- envelope_id: UUIDv4 (string)
- collector_id: string (syspath or resolver id)
- customer_id: string
- event_type: string (e.g., role.change, access.grant, key_rotation)
- timestamp_utc: ISO-8601
- sequence_hint: integer (monotonic per collector, best-effort)
- payload_schema: string (schema identifier or version)
- payload: base64 or compressed blob (depending on size)
- signature: optional JWS of payload using collector key (for high-sensitivity artifacts)
- provenance: list of short markers (collector_version, host_id, sha256(payload))
- retention_tier: string (hot|warm|cold)
- export_flags: list (siem, legal, forensics, analytics)

Transport & API behaviors:
- HTTP POST /v1/evidence/ingest for small events (idempotent by envelope_id).
- Kafka topic per-region for high-volume streaming; producers include envelope_id as key.
- Batches accepted up to 50 envelopes; server returns per-envelope status.
- Backpressure indicated via 429 with Retry-After and a structured retry-window header (ms).

Idempotency and dedupe:
- Primary dedupe: envelope_id dedupe lookup in orchestrator fast path (in-memory LRU + persistent tombstone in evidence-store with TTL equal to longest retention).
- Secondary dedupe for streaming: sequence_hint + collector_id used to detect out-of-order duplicates.

Authentication & RBAC notes (RBAC v2):
- Collectors use short-lived signed client tokens (scoped to customer_id and collector_id). Tokens include scopes: ingest:evidence, read:status.
- Orchestrator service account has export:stream and export:snapshot scopes; all export actions logged to audit stream with export_reason and operator_id.
- For high-sensitivity exports (legal/forensics), orchestrator must obtain an HSM-signed consent token or be on a allowlist enforced by the policy engine.
- Auditability: every token mint and scope usage is logged as a control-evidence event for downstream verification.

Export mapping to SIEM (practical guidance):
- Map envelope fields to SIEM event fields: envelope_id -> event_id, event_type -> event.type, timestamp_utc -> event.time, collector_id -> source.host, customer_id -> source.customer_id, sha256(payload) -> file.hash.
- For payloads exceeding SIEM size limits, store payload in Evidence Store and send pointer (evidence_store://<id>) + short summary in SIEM.
- Tag exported events with export_origin and export_policy_id for traceability.

Orchestration states and transitions (simple FSM):
- RECEIVED -> VALIDATED -> ENRICHED -> QUEUED_FOR_EXPORT -> EXPORTING -> EXPORTED | EXPORT_FAILED -> RETRY_BACKOFF -> MANUAL_ESCALATION -> ARCHIVED
- Each transition emits a control-evidence audit event. Retries implement exponential backoff with jitter and max_attempts config per export_policy.

Failure modes & operator playbook (common scenarios):
1) Duplicate delivery spikes from a flaky collector
   - Symptom: increased RECEIVED with same envelope_id, rate-limited 429s downstream.
   - Action: enable dedupe short-circuit, tag collector_id for remediation, throttle collector via token revoke. Raise ticket JIRA-SEC-XXXX.
2) Evidence store unavailable during large backfill
   - Symptom: QUEUED_FOR_EXPORT grows; EXPORT_FAILED for snapshot exports.
   - Action: promote warm-tier buffer retention, trigger regional fallback export (S3 fallback). Notify infra team and enable degraded-mode export.
3) SIEM ingestion schema changes causing mapping errors
   - Symptom: EXPORT_FAILED with 422 and schema mismatch reason.
   - Action: hold export, route to dead-letter queue for developer review, apply mapping transform in transform-service, replay.
4) Token misuse / unauthorized export
   - Symptom: unexpected export_origin or elevated export_policy_id seen in audit stream.
   - Action: revoke affected keys, perform forensic pull from Evidence Store for affected envelope_ids, open incident, notify compliance.

Monitoring & SLOs (suggested):
- Ingest success rate >= 99.95% (24h rolling)
- Median end-to-end export latency for high-priority events < 30s
- Lost evidence rate < 0.001% (measured by envelope tombstones vs receipts)
- Export failure alert if > 0.5% of exports in a region fail for > 30m

Instrumentation telemetry to emit:
- ingest.received.count, ingest.duplicate.count, ingest.validation.failure.count
- orchestrator.transition.<state>.count and orchestrator.transition.<state>.latency_ms_p50/p95
- export.sink.<sink_name>.success/count and export.sink.<sink_name>.failure/count
- evidence-store.put.latency_ms and evidence-store.replay.count

Backfill and replay strategy:
- Backfill runs use a dedicated backfill policy: throttled writes to Evidence Store, tag backfill:true, and export with export_policy_id=backfill-YYYYMMDD.
- Ensure replayed envelopes include original timestamp_utc and original_envelope_id to preserve audit lineage.
- Maintain backfill window metadata so audits can distinguish live vs replayed evidence.

Operational checklists (quick):
- Before major changes: run schema compatibility tests against SIEM sandbox; run end-to-end ingest -> export smoke test with representative payloads.
- Daily: monitor tombstone growth and duplicate rates; review any EXPORT_FAILED events in dead-letter queue older than 1h.
- Post-incident: produce forensics bundle with envelope_ids, orchestrator logs, token mint events, and export_policy config.

Open design questions / action items:
- Decide canonical payload encoding: base64 vs compressed JSON blob (action: engineering to benchmark both for common sizes)
- Define retention tiers quotas per-customer for evidence-store (action: product + legal to propose tiers and pricing)
- Add a lightweight signed proof-of-ingest (receipt) API to simplify customer verification claims (action: RFC draft by security).

Appendix: sample envelope (compact example)
{
  "envelope_id": "9f8c4b9a-2b7d-4c6f-8d1a-3a8f0e2c7b2f",
  "collector_id": "collector-east-03",
  "customer_id": "acct-12345",
  "event_type": "role.change",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-02-18T15:20:31Z",
  "sequence_hint": 1202,
  "payload_schema": "rbac-v2-role-change.v1",
  "payload": "{...compressed json...}",
  "signature": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...",
  "provenance": ["collector:v0.9.2","host:ip-10-0-1-22"],
  "retention_tier": "hot",
  "export_flags": ["siem","legal"]
}

Notes on uniqueness / compatibility: this playbook intentionally focuses on handoff semantics and operator remediation rather than low-level collector implementation details. It should be used alongside the existing collector SDK README and SIEM adapter mappings.

If you are reviewing: please comment on the open action items and add any missing failure modes you have observed in the last 6 months.
